title: Utility Service Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: An original utility service workflow that guides a bounded inspection from readiness through findings and release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete utility service inspection checklist form for the electric, gas, water, or thermal utility service point that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when an assigned inspector must confirm safe observation boundaries, document domain-specific conditions, route deficiencies, and record a qualified acceptance, restriction, or follow-up decision. The utility service coordinator owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Utility service inspection identity and authority
sections.guidance: Define the asset, inspection scope, qualified reviewer, and conditions before observations begin.

sections.title: Utility service readiness and safe observation boundary
sections.guidance: Confirm identity, operating context, access, and limits before checking condition.

blocks.label: Stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not use this record to approach downed conductors, investigate a gas odor, enter flooded electrical areas, operate unknown valves or switches, or bypass dispatch control. Keep people clear, use the organization's emergency route, and allow only qualified and authorized personnel to isolate, test, repair, and restore the affected utility service.

sections.title: Utility service inspection points and finding evidence
sections.guidance: Check each point only when observed; use the findings table for condition, evidence, and disposition.

blocks.label: Domain inspection checklist
items: Account, premise, commodity, meter, and service-point identities agree
Access conditions, traffic, animals, weather, and public exposure were assessed
Visible service equipment is intact, supported, labeled, and unobstructed
Leak, odor, arcing, heat, noise, vibration, corrosion, or damage is absent or escalated
Meter, display, seals, valves, regulators, and disconnects were observed without bypass
Representative service value and operating status were recorded with method
Customer equipment was distinguished from utility-owned equipment
Critical-load and affected-customer consequences were checked before interruption
Required outage, dispatch, operations, or emergency coordination was recorded
Before-and-after status and customer communication evidence were captured
Unresolved ownership, access, equipment, and service-quality issues have owners
Return-to-service decision was made by the designated qualified authority

fields.label: Inaccessible areas, sampling limits, representative conditions, trends, and supporting context

sections.title: Utility service exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Gas odor, hissing, suspected leak, or atmosphere concern
Downed conductor, arcing, exposed electrical part, or burn damage
Major water release, flooding, washout, or energized equipment in water
Steam, pressure, hot surface, rotating equipment, or uncontrolled stored energy
Traffic, excavation, unstable surface, animal, or uncontrolled public exposure
Unknown valve, switch, disconnect, cross-connection, or service ownership
Critical-load impact or service interruption without operations authorization
Condition requiring emergency dispatch or work beyond assigned qualification
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not use this record to approach downed conductors, investigate a gas odor, enter flooded electrical areas, operate unknown valves or switches, or bypass dispatch control. Keep people clear, use the organization's emergency route, and allow only qualified and authorized personnel to isolate, test, repair, and restore the affected utility service.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each inspection exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Utility service decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Electric, gas, water, or thermal utility service point identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
